clue.text: In a state, cats set off with Shamus

indicators.note: set off reads as departing, but off alone says these letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A private eye in some American state sees cats set off alongside him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shamus' is US slang for a private detective, which helps the American surface; here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is one of the New England states of the USA.

clue.text: For fuel economy, this writer's backing the French over tricky longer lap

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the French piece above what follows
backing tells us the contraction for this writer is is read in reverse

parts.note: this writer's is the setter saying I am, contracted to IM
les is the French plural definite article

indicators.note: tricky signals that the words longer lap are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone driving a tricky longer lap is thinking about fuel economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is I'M, which 'backing' turns to MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's fuel consumption is quoted as a distance travelled per unit of fuel, the standard economy measure.

clue.text: Exclusive store found below end of bypass

indicators.note: in a down clue, found below places the store piece under the bypass letter
end of picks out the final letter of the word bypass

parts.note: a co-op is a cooperative store

explanation.surface: A shop sits just past the end of the bypass road.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalistic exclusive is a story one paper gets before its rivals, a scoop.

clue.text: Chum's introduced to lady in pants showing vivacity

indicators.note: introduced to means the friend is put inside the other letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, so it signals lady and in are jumbled

parts.note: a chum is a mate, a friend; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A friend meets a lady wearing trousers, who is very lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, but as British slang for 'rubbish' it signals a jumble, giving ANIDLY; 'introduced to' then puts the friend inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting animatedly means behaving with liveliness and spirit, which is vivacity.

clue.text: One clashes with snob

definitions.meaning: a hi-hat is a pair of drum-kit cymbals struck together by a pedal

explanation.surface: A drummer's cymbal player looks down on everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The drum-kit cymbal pair is the hi-hat, and a haughty person who looks down on others is a high-hat.

clue.text: I may include last cutting from hazel in planter

indicators.note: include means one letter goes inside the compiler's title

parts.note: the person writing the clue, I, is the crossword compiler, the setter

indicators.note: last cutting from takes the final letter of the word hazel

explanation.surface: A gardener says she may add a hazel cutting to her planter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the crossword compiler, the SETTER, which takes the L from 'hazel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter in the historical sense is a colonist who settles new land, a settler.

clue.text: Carriage factor's looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a factor is a component, a part; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A factor sees business improving for the carriage trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Ruling out of overfishing could be smashing

indicators.note: ruling out says certain letters are removed from the longer word
could be says the remaining letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: the word of supplies the letters taken away

explanation.surface: A ban on overfishing would be a splendid thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O and F, the letters of 'of', from OVERFISHING and rearrange what remains. 'smashing' looks like 'splendid' but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver something is to break it into fragments, so shivering is breaking to pieces.

clue.text: Getting dangerously full, feed on substitute mainly, refined and graded

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the feed piece above the rest

parts.note: to sup is to take food or drink

indicators.note: mainly means the substitute word loses its last letter

parts.note: ersatz means an inferior substitute
U means upper-class, hence refined, in old British usage
graded means rated, given a grade

explanation.surface: An ersatz feed, refined and graded, leaves someone dangerously full.
explanation.walkthrough: ERSATZ without its last letter gives ERSAT. U for upper-class, and so refined, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A supersaturated solution holds more solute than it normally could, an unstable, overfull state.

clue.text: Investigating facilities with ruler, Andy's thwarted initially

parts.note: the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet, British loo
a king is a ruler

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of Andy's and thwarted

explanation.surface: A monarch called Andy is frustrated by the state of the toilets being inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at a matter is examining or considering it, which is investigating.

clue.text: Cheers may emerge from venue, I daresay, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
emerge from says the answer comes out of the run of letters in the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Applause might break out at a venue, one supposes, when people think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Cheers may emerge' as the definition, leaving the hidden word with no indicator; the definition is 'Cheers' alone, 'may' a link and 'emerge from' the hidden signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is British informal for goodbye, and adieu is the French farewell used in English.

clue.text: Month I lay naked in the shade

parts.note: Sep is the short form of September

indicators.note: naked means the word lay is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sunbather lies naked in the shade for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, a shade, from old photographs.

clue.text: Jerry's 25 sounds perfect

indicators.note: sounds says the word for perfect is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: whole means complete, perfect, undamaged

explanation.surface: Jerry, writing about an answer elsewhere, says it sounds perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerry is the mouse of Tom and Jerry cartoons; 25 is the answer to 25-down, so Jerry's dwelling is a mousehole.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon mouse lives in a little opening in the skirting board, his dwelling.

clue.text: Twice self-employed in cultural unit

indicators.note: twice says the pronoun for self is written two times

parts.note: me is the pronoun for oneself

explanation.surface: A self-employed person works in a cultural field.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Dawkins coined the term for a unit of culture passed from person to person.

clue.text: Glassware in factory fire — oil mostly involved

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: involved means twisted, so fire and the trimmed oil are mixed
mostly means the word oil loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out at a glassworks with oil feeding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil mostly' is OI; FIRE plus OI, mixed up, gives EFIORI.
explanation.definitionFit: Millefiori is decorative Italian glasswork made of fused coloured rods, 'a thousand flowers'.

clue.text: Apart from one, trainees developed promise

indicators.note: apart from says a letter is excluded from the longer word
developed signals the remaining letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: With one exception, the trainees showed real potential.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from TRAINEES and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a token or pledge given as an assurance of more to come.

clue.text: Puddle contents getting artist immersed?

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist
immersed means plunged in water

explanation.surface: A painter has stepped in a puddle and got soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RA IN WATER, an artist immersed.
explanation.definitionFit: A puddle is a small pool of water left on the ground after rainfall.

clue.text: Fruit, two-thirds produced in south

indicators.note: two-thirds means only four of the six letters are kept

parts.note: raised means grown, produced
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two-thirds of the fruit is grown in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are dried grapes, a type of dried fruit.

clue.text: Field-guide displays footwear

definitions.meaning: in Scotland, a gillie is an attendant guiding someone hunting or fishing
a laced shoe without a tongue, worn with Highland dress

explanation.surface: A field guide shows off his shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish sporting attendant and the tongueless laced dance shoe share this name.

clue.text: Peacock's marking vacant essay on obscure poets

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second
vacant means the word essay is emptied, keeping its outside letters
obscure signals that the word poets is jumbled

explanation.surface: An empty essay about obscure poets mentions a peacock.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacock's tail feathers bear round eye-like spots of colour.

clue.text: Joy's sidelight is going west, going west!

indicators.note: going west, as slang for vanishing, says those letters disappear from the longer word
going west, in an across clue, reads the word is from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted that a car's sidelight has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'going west' turns IS into SI; the second, slang for perishing, takes SI out of SIDELIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Dry up with Mr James in muddle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the joined words for dry and Mr James are read from bottom to top

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
Sid James was a British comic actor, star of the Carry On films

explanation.surface: Dry up, says someone to Mr James, who is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr James is Sid James, a British comedy actor of the Carry On films. BRUT plus SID, turned by 'up', gives the answer. 'Dry up' looks like a phrase telling someone to stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb papers or plans is to throw them into disorder, to muddle them.

clue.text: Police ultimately detain grass

parts.note: the law is a slang term for the police

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of detain

explanation.surface: The police finally arrest an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is an area of mown grass.

clue.text: Joins in midweek?

definitions.meaning: to join in marriage is to marry
an informal short form for on Wednesdays, the middle of the week

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in something halfway through the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying is joining two people, and the abbreviated plural of Wednesday means on those days.

clue.text: Faculty's just outside Lima

indicators.note: outside says the word for just goes around the letter for Lima

parts.note: fair means just, equitable
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A university faculty sits just outside the Peruvian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a natural talent or aptitude, a flair.

clue.text: It's awful, half the content of charity sale going to Grand Hotel

indicators.note: going to sets the hotel letters after the sale piece
half the content of keeps only the second half of the word for a charity sale

parts.note: a bazaar is a sale of goods for charity
G is short for grand, a thousand
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A charity sale is held at the Grand Hotel, and it's dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep AAR, the back half of BAZAAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression of horror or frustration someone cries when something is terrible.

clue.text: Stop the setter in Habitat — this could be stolen from 1ac, 15, 18, 23, 2, 5 or 7

parts.note: ho is a call to halt, as to horses
the setter refers to the compiler as me

explanation.surface: The compiler stops in a Habitat furniture store, where something could be stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball a runner can steal home; the answers listed each make a phrase with the answer (home state, home field and so on).
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's habitat is the place where it lives naturally, its natural dwelling.

clue.text: Overcome with locusts regularly at party

indicators.note: regularly picks out every second letter of locusts

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone is overcome by locusts at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to beat or surpass them, to overcome.

clue.text: Underworld boss's tailless old plane maybe given to tycoon

parts.note: Pluto is the Roman god ruling the underworld

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, ramshackle aircraft or car

explanation.surface: A crime boss gives an old plane to a business tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power comes from wealth, like a rich tycoon.

clue.text: Trees Basil damaged he and daughter made good again

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of trees and Basil are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Basil damaged the trees, and he and his daughter repaired them.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-establish something is to restore it, set it up again.
